questions.prompt: Which command restores a file from the previous commit without moving HEAD?
questions.explanation: `git restore --source=HEAD~1 file.txt` restores one file from the previous commit; `restore` never moves HEAD.

questions.prompt: Which of the three commands changes history?
questions.explanation: `git reset` rewrites branch history; `git revert` creates a new commit instead; `git restore` works on files only.

questions.prompt: You want to undo the latest commit but keep its changes staged, ready to recommit. Which command?
questions.explanation: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` moves HEAD back one commit and keeps the changes staged.

questions.prompt: What is the default mode of `git reset HEAD~1`?
options: `--mixed`: moves HEAD back and unstages, keeping the file edits
questions.explanation: `--mixed` is the default: HEAD moves back, changes are unstaged but the file edits stay.
